Aggregate symptoms in symptom table to work out ILI etc.

Source: R/aggregate_symptoms.r
aggregate_symptoms.Rd

The recorded onset is kept in the column onset: "sudden", "not.sudden", "dont_know" (an explicit answer), "not.answered" (the question was asked but not answered) or "no.question" (the data have no onset question). None of the last three establishes sudden onset. ili.sudden.unknown sets how the last three are interpreted in the derived columns suddenly, ili and ili.fever. It leaves onset and the answers in the data unchanged. A report that already fails another ILI criterion is not ILI, whatever its onset.

Usage

aggregate_symptoms(symptoms, ili.sudden.unknown = NA)

Arguments

symptoms

a data table of symptom reports

ili.sudden.unknown

how to interpret reports where onset is unknown (see above): NA (the default) leaves suddenly, ili and ili.fever missing where onset is needed to decide, 1 counts unknown onset as sudden and 0 counts it as not sudden.

Value

a data table with added columns, including onset

Author

seb
